rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent single mass in all four views, so it clears basic continuity and repair integrity, but it remains fundamentally a sealed rectangular block with only a small, semantically weak ground notch. The dominant gesture is clear, yet the open-space figure is not: the blue frontage edge is acknowledged only indirectly, and there is no convincing public court, entry seam, terrace, or undercut tying the mass to the verified access edge. For neighborhood living, the visible mass must support an active ground threshold and a clear public-space relation; here the section is too generic and the upper body simply sits on the base without an expressive public void or access-oriented articulation. Reference set points toward courtyard/bridge/terrace strategies, but the current candidate has not yet converted that language into a legible program relation. Thus it is formally coherent but programmatically underfit.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact low-rise mass with a strong carved central void and a bridging upper connection can create a legible community-building threshold.
